newsitem.title: USA: Visioneering settles fraud accusations with CFTC.
newsitem.headline: Visioneering settles fraud accusations with CFTC.

text.p: A Las Vegas-based company agreed to pay a $50,000 fine to settle accusations that it distorted the performance record for two managed account programs, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission said Wednesday.
Visioneering Research and Development Co also gave the inaccurate information to industry trade publications, the CFTC said.
Visioneering, a registered commodity trading advisor, caused the performance record of its V-150 program and V-SP500 program to reflect client investment in months when there was none.
Robert Everson, the firm's president, also entered into the settlement for the violations that occurred from November 1994 through February 1997, the CFTC said.

Visioneering did not admit or deny the findings but agreed to pay a $50,000 civil penalty as part of the settlement. The company also agreed to name a compliance officer to review Visioneering disclosure documents for accuracy.
